name: Liraglutide

lead: Liraglutide is a GLP-1 receptor agonist from Novo Nordisk, given as a daily injection. It was approved as Victoza for type 2 diabetes and, at a higher strength, as Saxenda for chronic weight management; it was the first GLP-1 drug approved for obesity treatment.

Its weight-loss effect is more modest than that of semaglutide or tirzepatide, with average losses in trials of roughly 5 to 8 percent of body weight. It is now of mainly historical or niche interest in fat-loss circles, as newer agents with larger reported effects have largely replaced it.

paras: Liraglutide is a GLP-1 analogue with a fatty-acid chain that promotes albumin binding and gives it a half-life of about 13 hours, allowing once-daily dosing. By activating GLP-1 receptors it increases satiety, delays gastric emptying and enhances glucose-dependent insulin release, which lowers calorie intake and body weight.

Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea and constipation are the usual complaints, with gallbladder events, pancreatitis and raised heart rate reported less often. It carries a boxed warning about thyroid C-cell tumours in rodents. Weight is commonly regained when the drug is stopped, and it requires daily injections. It is prescription-only.
